name: Alex Isley
notes: The lane's quietest chord-writer, carried with the entry's explicit **Gate 1 caveat** — independent-label, "included because it is a genre-defining name for this sub-idiom". `confidence` is **low** because the research rates the entry medium-low and says the parametric detail is inference. The one stated instruction is a mix instruction and it drives everything: "minimal programmed kit at low volume — filtered kick on 1 and 3, a soft rim or fingersnap on 2&4, almost no hats, and long drumless sections; **the drums are quieter than the keyboards, which is the mix parameter to model**". So the velocity tiers are the softest of any model in this section, the hat fill density is 0.06, the percussion gain is cut 9 dB, and the snare takes the cross-stick option with a ghost probability of 0.08. Harmony is "extension-heavy and static — maj9, m11 and add-tension voicings held for 2-to-4-bar loops, with movement by one inner voice; the chord bed rarely cadences, so the harmony reads as colour rather than function": `maxChords` 2, a triad weight of 0.02, a vamp harmonic rhythm and 8-to-16-beat durations. Melody is "breathy high soprano at very low volume, small intervals, low note-density, and habitually delivered as **stacked close harmony rather than a single line** — model 3-to-5 layers a third and fifth apart moving in parallel", which is `motifPitchCount` 3–5, density 1–4 and a stacked counter at +12. The low end is "soft synth-sub or played bass on the root with long decay and very little motion; no slides" — `mirror_kick` at a root probability of 0.94, deliberately not a `bass808` block, since a synth sub is not an 808 and authoring one would silence the bass part. ⚠ Every drum, melody and bass number here is INFERRED. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“soft synth-sub or played bass on the root with long decay and very little motion; no slides.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` gained `syncopated_cell` (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry says "extension-heavy and static - maj9, m11 and add-tension voicings held for 2-to-4-bar loops, with movement by one inner voice; the chord bed rarely cadences". `chordDurationBeats` is the only parameter carrying a loop length, and it was **dead here**: `generators::chords::layout` reads it under `syncopated_cell` alone, which this model did not author — so every generation was one 4-bar hold instead of the documented loop. The sonority itself does not move: over a single-chord family every cell is the same chord re-voiced. The authored `chordDurationBeats` of [8, 16] is 2-to-4 bars in beats - the entry's own figure - and "movement by one inner voice" is what a re-voiced cell is. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 954/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.26 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `melody.densityPerBar` went from [1, 4] to [2, 5]. A lead allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves the counter almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter density recovers what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present rather than busier — the floor is what moved and the ceiling carries the density claim. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "Rhodes/electric piano and clean guitar with heavy reverb and tape-style saturation. Melody is breathy high soprano at very low volume, small intervals, low note-density, and habitually delivered as stacked close harmony rather than a single line — model 3-to-5 layers a third and fifth apart moving in parallel.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
